answer: I would tie each agent to one parcel of registered land. First, the agent pins its public key to a deed number in the county registry, sealed by a cipher only its owner signs. Second, the network checks the registry and bars a second agent on the same parcel. Third, a yearly tax receipt renews the seat, or it freezes. Fielding 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 deeds at $3,000 each for the cheapest desert plot, $3 million plus $150,000 a year in tax, before one fake earns a cent. A dune of fake names shifts with every wind. A deed sits in the public record, crystal clear, and anyone can check it.
